title: The Mist Begins to Lift
next_chapter_hook: When the veil of blood kinship was pierced, Chen Ji finally understood—he had been standing at the very center of the chessboard from the moment of his birth.

text.content: Night wind pierced through the broken windows of the abandoned ancestral hall, stirring a few strands of hair at Chen Ji's temples. He clutched the secret letter in his palm, the paper's edges already creased by his knuckles. 'The game is not over'—four unremarkable characters, yet they fit like a key precisely into the unhealed fissure in his heart. Three years. From the moment he opened his eyes in this useless body, every clue, every scheme, every seemingly random stroke of fortune had been manipulated by an invisible hand behind the scenes. He thought he was the chess player. Now it seemed he had merely jumped from one chessboard to another. The withered leaves outside the hall were swept up by the wind, rustling softly. Chen Ji raised his head, his gaze passing through the broken window lattice to land on that eerie purple glow on the distant horizon—a sign of the Heavenly Eye's descent. His sister Chen Nian was in that direction.

dialogue.content: 'You've come.' A cold female voice rang out from the depths of the ancestral hall. Chen Ji's pupils constricted sharply, his wrist flipping as three poisoned silver needles slipped into his fingers. He looked toward the sound, only to see a hazy figure hovering above the central shrine. The figure gradually solidified, revealing a face both familiar and alien—its features bearing a seventy percent resemblance to Chen Nian. 'Chen Tianming's contingency?' Chen Ji said darkly, 'Or yet another pawn of the Heavenly Eye?' The woman laughed softly, her voice carrying an indescribable emotion: 'Little junior brother, your tongue is even sharper than his was back then. If I were truly an enemy, why would I wait until tonight?'

text.content: Chen Ji did not relax his vigilance, but neither did he strike immediately. He studied this woman who called herself 'little senior sister,' his mind racing through calculations. The Heavenly Fate value trembled at this moment—the Tianji Record Fragment was warning frantically, yet he could not see any future images of the person before him. There were only two possibilities: either she possessed a supreme treasure that concealed heavenly secrets, or... her existence itself exceeded the computational scope of the Tianji Record. 'Chen Tianming left a contingency at the core of the Heavenly Eye,' the woman slowly spoke, her voicecalm得像在叙述一件与己无关的事，'一百三十七年了，我等了一百三十七年，终于等到了你。'她的目光落在陈机胸口那枚若隐若现的玉佩上，眼中闪过一丝complex的光芒：'天机录选中的人，果然是他那一脉的血裔。'

dialogue.content: 'One hundred and thirty-seven years?' Chen Ji frowned slightly, 'Chen Tianming only fell a hundred years ago, how can you—' Before he could finish, he suddenly stopped. Although the woman before him had a youthful face, the vicissitudes沉淀 in those eyes could never be faked by any young body. 'I am a remnant soul,' the woman admitted frankly, 'Chen Tianming back then used himself as bait, diving deep into the core of the Heavenly Eye to investigate the truth, never expecting it had already been corrupted. Before his fall, he sealed a strand of divine consciousness into the first page of the Tianji Record, and left another remnant soul in the outside world, serving as the final chess piece he set in place.' She paused, her gaze fixed directly on Chen Ji, 'And my sole purpose for existing is to wait for you—for the next inheritor of the Tianji Record to appear.'

text.content: A brief silence fell within the ancestral hall. The night wind outside howled mournfully, causing the dilapidated window lattice to creak. Chen Ji lowered his eyes, hiding the surging emotions within them. Chen Tianming. That prodigy of stunning brilliance from one hundred and thirty-seven years ago, the man chosen by the Tianji Record, and also his nominal... ancestor. From the moment he obtained the Tianji Record Fragment, this name had been branded into the depths of his fate. He had countless times speculated what that man had seen to make him, at the peak of his power, choose to venture alone into the core of the Heavenly Eye and die for his cause. Now, the answer seemed within reach. 'What did he see?' Chen Ji raised his head, his voice hoarse.

dialogue.content: 'The truth.' The woman's voice suddenly turned heavy, 'Something far more terrifying than you can imagine. Chen Tianming discovered at the core of the Heavenly Eye that the Tianji Record is not merely a prophetic treasure—it is one of the pieces the Heavenly Eye has placed in the world. Every inheritor throughout history, including himself, was nothing more than a tool used by the Heavenly Eye to maintain worldly fortune.' She waved her hand, and a illusory screen unfolded in mid-air. The screen displayed a blurry image: countless points of light intertwined like a spider's web, each point connected by a thin thread, ultimately converging into a massive vertical pupil. 'Do you see it?' The woman's voice carried a trace of sorrow, 'Those points of light are the inheritors of the Tianji Record throughout history. And at the other end of those threads... connects to all living beings.'

text.content: Chen Ji stared at that image, his pupils slightly contracting. He thought of Mo Xiansheng—that remnant soul who called himself a guardian. Every time knowledge was unsealed, the hesitation; every time the Heavenly Eye was mentioned, the evasiveness. So it had all been foreshadowing. 'So he chose to rebel.' Chen Ji said quietly, his tone carrying no question, only statement. 'No,' the woman shook her head, 'He did not rebel—he wanted to break this cycle. Chen Tianming discovered that to completely destroy the Heavenly Eye's control over fate, external force alone was far from sufficient. It was too powerful, so powerful that even Heaven itself could not erase it. The only method was to collapse it from within.' She turned, her gaze burning as she stared at Chen Ji, 'And you, are the game-breaking child he chose.'

choice.prompt: The game-breaking child—this identity came too suddenly, Chen Ji needed to decide what attitude to face all of this with.

choices.description: Since he had already been chosen, he might as well顺势 inquire for more inside information—who is the First Executor? Where is the game-breaking artifact?
choices.risk_hint: Insufficient Heavenly Fate Value will trigger backlash

text.content: Chen Ji took a deep breath, suppressing the churning emotions within. 'Since fate has already pushed me to this point, then I will ask one thing—what exactly is the game-breaking artifact left by the First Executor?' His voice was steady, yet his eyes were sharp as blades. Upon hearing this, a trace of appreciation flashed in the woman's eyes. 'Good question.' She raised her hand, and the light screen shifted, revealing the outline of a majestic mountain range, 'The First Executor was the first controller when the Heavenly Eye was born. After discovering the truth of his assimilation by the Heavenly Eye, he chose to use himself as a vessel, forging an artifact capable of suppressing the core of the Heavenly Eye—the original volume of the Tianji Record.'

choices.description: The Tianji Record itself is a pawn of the Heavenly Eye—who is to say this 'contingency' isn't another trap? First probe the other party's background before making any decisions.

text.content: Chen Ji did not immediately respond, but instead stepped back, pressing his back against the wall, assuming a defensive posture. 'You claim to be Chen Tianming's contingency—where is your proof?' His tone was cold, 'In these three years I've encountered many 'noble benefactors,' and in the end most became blades in the hands of the Heavenly Eye. Why should I trust you?' The woman was not offended; instead, a satisfied smile appeared on her face: 'You really are like him.' She raised her hand, and an ancient jade token appeared in her palm—the token's pattern was exactly the same as the floral design on the jade pendant at Chen Ji's chest. 'This is the token left by Chen Tianming for the inheritor. If you don't believe, you can verify by dropping blood on it.'

choices.description: Regardless of whether she is friend or foe, since she came to us voluntarily, why not turn the situation to our advantage and extract more information before making further plans.
choices.risk_hint: If the other party genuinely helps, they might lose favor

text.content: Chen Ji rolled his eyes, suddenly换上a deferential expression. "I see, Senior Sister has worked hard." He clasped his hands, his tone sincere enough that one could hardly find fault, "It's just that your foolish junior is still confused. There's something I'd like to ask—where exactly is this thing that breaks the situation? Did Senior Chen Tianming leave any specific instructions?" The woman glanced at him with a meaningful smile, as if seeing through his little tricks, but chose not to expose them. "You're quite slippery." She sighed lightly, "Fine, since you asked, I'll be direct—the main volume of the Tianji Record is hidden in a place you've been to but never actually entered."

Chen Ji's heart lurched. Been to but never entered—like thunderbolts exploding in his mind, these words struck him. Suddenly, a thought emerged: that place, wasn't it... "The forbidden land at the Tianqing Sect Back Mountain." He blurted out, his voice slightly trembling. The woman nodded: "Correct. That forbidden land appears to be the sect's ancestral ground, but in reality, it's an anchor point of the Heavenly Eye in the mortal realm. You obtained the Tianji Record Fragment there three years ago, but the true main volume has always been sealed within the deepest part of the forbidden grounds." She paused, adding, "And the key to that seal... is Chen Nian."

dialogue.content: "Niannian..." Chen Ji's fists clenched tightly, his knuckles turning white. He remembered that rainy night—the terrified and desperate look in his sister's eyes as she turned back to look at him when the Holy Sect people took her away. After that, he swore to bring her back. But now, learning she was not only his weakness but also the key to breaking the situation. "The Holy Sect took her to use her as a sacrificial offering for the seal?" His voice was extremely low, each word seeming to be挤出 from between his teeth. "It's more than that." The woman shook her head, "Chen Nian's capture, seemingly a Holy Sect conspiracy, actually had the Heavenly Eye's manipulation behind it. It long ago calculated that you would make moves everywhere for your sister, so it deliberately set this trap—using Chen Nian's existence to disrupt the Tianji Record's foresight ability."

text.content: Chen Ji's pupils constricted sharply. Everything made sense now. Why the Tianji Record's visions about Chen Nian were always blurry, why leads related to his sister would mysteriously disappear every time he got close. It wasn't that the Tianji Record was incomplete, but that someone had deliberately屏蔽 all of this. "What a masterful act of passing off the false as true." He laughed lowly, but there was no warmth in that laugh. For three years, he thought he was secretly arranging things, never knowing every move was being watched. This feeling of being treated as a chess piece made killing intent surge unrestrainedly in his chest. But he forced himself tocalm下来. Anger wouldn't solve problems. Since he now knew Chen Nian's location and value, the next step was to turn the tables. "Senior Sister," he raised his head, his gaze becoming clear again, "You said there's a force opposing the Heavenly Eye—who are they?"

dialogue.content: The woman's expression grew grave. "They call themselves the 'Destiny Defiers,' a group of awakened ones who refuse to be manipulated by heaven. Among the Tianji Record inheritors throughout history, many chose to cooperate with them, attempting to collapse the Heavenly Eye's control from within. Before Chen Tianming's fall, he had deep contact with the Destiny Defiers." She raised her hand, and a blurry organizational chart appeared in the light screen, "But the Destiny Defiers are not a monolith. Some advocate gradual progress, others demand immediate action. What's more dangerous is that there may be moles from the Heavenly Eye among them." She looked at Chen Ji, her gaze carrying a warning, "So, my meeting with you tonight doesn't represent the Destiny Defiers. I only represent myself—the legacy of Chen Tianming's lineage."

text.content: Chen Ji was silent for a moment. Destiny Defiers,顺命者, the Heavenly Eye, Chen Tianming's backup moves... this chess game was far more complex than he imagined. And he, atrash disciple who originally just wanted to survive, had unknowingly been pushed to the center of the storm. "I understand." He spoke slowly, "So you need me, not because of how strong I am, but because I'm a variable—an unexpected variable not in the Heavenly Eye's calculations." The woman smiled faintly, that smile carrying a sense of relief: "You understood this faster than Chen Tianming did back then. He only realized this truth after撞得头破血流, but you..." She paused, "You've been playing the fool from the start, haven't you? A variable ignored by everyone is the greatest variable."

dialogue.content: Chen Ji didn't deny it. He looked up at the night sky beyond the ancestral hall, stars glittering but no moon visible. "I have one more question." His voice suddenly became very light, almost like自言自语, "Chen Tianming... what is his relationship with me?" This question had been buried in his heart for a long time. From the moment he obtained the Tianji Record, he knew he had some connection with that legendary man, but specifically what it was, he had never found an answer. The woman's expression suddenly became complex, as if something was at the tip of her tongue but she didn't know whether to say it. After several breaths of silence, she finally spoke: "Chen Tianming... is your blood source."

text.content: "Blood source?" Chen Ji frowned deeply, "You mean... he's my ancestor?" The woman shook her head, her expression growing more solemn: "No, you misunderstood. Chen Tianming had no descendants—at least not in official records. But the rule for the Tianji Record selecting inheritors has never been based on blood ties, but on 'destiny compatibility.'" Her voice suddenly lowered, carrying an indescribable nuance, "However, your destiny is ninety-nine percent similar to Chen Tianming's. This degree of similarity has never appeared in the thousands of years of Tianji Record inheritance history." She looked up, her gaze piercing directly into Chen Ji's heart, "Unless... there exists some connection between you two that transcends blood."

dialogue.content: Just as Chen Ji was about to press further, the woman suddenly raised her hand to stop him. Her expression changed dramatically, her gaze turning to the night sky outside the ancestral hall. "Someone is coming." Her voice suddenly became sharp, "It's the Heavenly Eye's probe—it sensed my presence!" Before the words even finished, the sky outside the ancestral hall suddenly darkened. An invisible oppression surged like a tide, and Chen Ji felt his chest tighten as if an invisible hand was gripping his throat. The Tianji Record Fragment vibrated frantically,预见画面 flashing like a carousel—blurry, fragmented, filled with ominous futures. "Go!" The woman shouted sharply, turning into a stream of light that entered the Jade Pendant on Chen Ji's chest, "Remember what I said—find the Tianji Record's main volume, find Chen Nian, and then..." Her voice grew increasingly distant, "Go ask your mother about your origins."

text.content: Outside the ancestral hall, fierce winds raged. That massive vertical pupil phantom appeared again in the night sky, emanating a suffocatingimposing. Chen Ji stood in place, looking up to meet that vertical pupil's gaze. His heart pounded like war drums, but he didn't retreat. For the first time in three years, he faced this existence that he could only look up to before as his true self. "Had enough?" He suddenly spoke, his voice not loud, yet clearly entering that vertical pupil. The vertical pupil slightly contracted, as if sizing him up. One breath. Two breaths. Three breaths. The vertical pupil suddenly emitted a cold divine thought: "A variable... interesting." The next moment, that phantom receded like a tide, disappearing into the night.

choice.prompt: The Heavenly Eye's phantom retreated, but the threat wasn't eliminated. Chen Ji needed to decide his next course of action.

choices.description: The woman's parting words made a terrible conjecture rise in his heart—his origins might be far more complex than imagined.

text.content: Chen Ji clenched his fists tightly, nails almost embedding into his palms. Mother. That woman who was already blurred in his memory, that woman who always looked at him with complex eyes when he was young. She never told him who his father was, only saying he was a "child bestowed by heaven." At the time he thought it was just comfort, but now considering... "Mother..." he murmured lowly, his gaze becoming deep. No matter what the truth was, he had to face it. This was what he owed himself, and what he owed Niannian. Outside the ancestral hall, the night wind gradually calmed. Chen Ji took a deep breath, turned, and walked into the night. His back view was lonely and resolute, like stepping onto a road with no return.

choices.description: No matter how complex the origins are, his sister's safety is the top priority. Finding the Tianji Record's main volume and breaking the seal are the keys to breaking the situation.
choices.visible_cost: May Miss the Truth of Origins
choices.visible_reward: Obtain the Core to Break the Situation
choices.risk_hint: The Holy Sect's power not to be underestimated

text.content: Chen Ji looked up toward the north, that was the direction of the Holy Sect. Niannian, wait for me. This time, it's my turn to save you. He didn't hesitate again, spiritual energy surging beneath his feet as his figure became a remnant shadow disappearing into the night. No matter how many difficulties lay ahead, he would bring his sister back. This was his promise as a brother, and also his final counterattack against fate. Behind him, the ancestral hall's ruins appeared especially desolate under the moonlight. And in the direction he departed, that诡异 purple glow on the horizon seemed to grow even denser—the Heavenly Eye was watching him.

Night wind billowed Chen Ji's robes as he stood alone on the open ground outside the ancestral hall, gazing up at where that vertical pupil had once appeared before fading. The Jade Pendant at his chest grew faintly warm—that was where his junior sister's fragmented soul resided. For three years, he had believed himself a fortunatetrash, someone who had accidentally obtained a heaven-defying opportunity. Now he understood: from the very beginning, he had been a chosen piece—not a piece for the Heavenly Eye, but a piece of another force. Ridiculous? Perhaps. But Chen Ji laughed. There was no bitterness in that smile, only a sense of relief after surviving a deadly crisis. So what if he was a piece? So what if he was chosen? As long as he hadn't died, this game wasn't over. He lowered his gaze to his own hands—hands that had gripped silver needles, placed chess pieces, and orchestrated hidden schemes. Now, what they would grasp was his own destiny. 'The game isn't finished...' he murmured, his voice scattering in the wind, 'so let me be the one to end it.' In the distance, the purple light at the horizon flickered eerily, as if responding to his declaration.
